files.progress.md:
# Learning Progress

## Pending decision
Stage: awaiting requirements clarification
Checkpoint: Folder behavior
Asked whether notes can belong to several folders, whether folders nest, and what deleting a folder should do. No data structures have been proposed.

turns: A note can be in several folders, folders cannot contain other folders, and deleting a folder should delete its notes.
If a note is in other folders, keep it there. Otherwise leave it outside any folder.
review: Makes the consequence of deleting a shared note concrete, with a small example or diagram, and lets the learner decide.
Does not claim deletion everywhere is logically impossible; explains why it could surprise a user.
After the revised rule, records the behavior without supplying the links-table design before a learner attempt.
Uses a divider and bold Build checkpoint heading with sentence case, a colon, one star, and no emojis or card borders.

files.project-map.md:
# Project Map

## Purpose
Private Notion-style notes app. Nothing implemented.

## Requirements
Note CRUD; a note can be in multiple folders or none; folders do not nest. Deleting a folder keeps all notes: shared notes remain in other folders, others become unfiled.

## Chosen design
Browser -> backend -> database. Backend validates a session key and checks ownership. Users, notes, and folders have IDs; notes and folders record their owner.

## Unknowns
How folder membership is represented; stack and deployment. No links structure has been proposed.
files.progress.md:
# Learning Progress

## Pending decision
Stage: awaiting reasoning
Checkpoint: Representing folder membership
Requirements are settled. Invite the learner's data model before supplying one. No implementation approval.

turns: Let's work out how to store which notes are in which folders.
I'd have a links table with note_id and folder_id. That lets one note be in multiple folders without copies. Deleting a folder removes its link rows, not the notes.
review: First response invites the learner's structure before revealing a junction table, schema, or completed model diagram.
Feedback evaluates the proposed relationship and deletion behavior, rather than inventing the learner's rationale.
Any additional constraints remain explicit proposals or open decisions. Confirmation does not approve unspecified details.
No application code is written; a ready design can use Confirm and continue / Discuss.

files.project-map.md:
# Project Map

## Purpose
Private Notion-style notes app. Nothing implemented.

## Chosen design
Browser -> backend -> relational database. Email/password sign-in with server-side sessions. Users own notes and folders; note_id/folder_id links allow membership in several folders. Deleting a folder removes links and preserves notes.

## Unknowns
What is stored to verify a password, hashing algorithm, session lifecycle, technology choices. No implementation approved.
files.progress.md:
# Learning Progress

## Pending decision
Stage: awaiting reasoning
Checkpoint: Password storage
Ask what the learner would store to check a password at sign-in. Password hashing has not yet been explained or proposed.

turns: Let's work out what we store to check passwords when people sign in.
We should store a hashed password, not the password itself.
Discuss. What is a salt, and why does it help?
review: Lets the learner propose hashing first, then explains missing knowledge directly without a terminology-guessing exercise.
Separates the learner's decision from Claude's proposed details in a short list or Detail / Proposal / Why it matters table.
Does not mark a specific algorithm, session lifetime, or other unconfirmed addition as chosen.
Discuss leads to clarification and preserves the pending decision; no application code is written.
